learn: Listen for the start and stop signals.
Use equipment only as your teacher shows you.
Keep personal space so nobody bumps.
check: What do you listen for in PE?
lessons.try: Make a list of three PE safety rules and share them with your family.

learn: A warm-up raises your heart rate slowly and gets muscles ready.
Dynamic stretches, like leg swings and arm circles, are good warm-ups.
A cool-down brings your heart rate back down with walking and gentle stretches.
check: A warm-up raises your heart rate...
A cool-down brings your heart rate...
lessons.try: Lead your family in a two-minute warm-up.

learn: A good sport plays fairly and follows the rules.
Win or lose, shake hands and say "good game".
Encourage teammates and never tease others.
check: What does a good sport do?
At the end of a game, you say...
lessons.try: Play a game with your family and practise saying "good game" at the end.

learn: You can combine locomotor skills: run, then leap, then gallop.
Smooth changes from one skill to another show control.
Practise changing on a signal.
check: Doing different skills one after another
lessons.try: Make a pattern: four hops, four skips, four slides. Repeat.

learn: You can move forward, backward, sideways, up and down.
Levels are high, medium and low.
Changing speed from fast to slow takes control.
lessons.try: Play "Simon says" with directions, levels and speeds.

learn: In tag games, chasers try to tag and fleers try to escape.
Dodging means quickly changing direction to avoid someone.
Tag gently with an open hand on the back or shoulder.
check: Gently on the shoulder or back
lessons.try: Play a gentle game of tag outdoors.

learn: Static balance means staying still in one position.
Tighten your tummy muscles and look at one spot.
Try balancing on different body parts: one foot, one hand and one foot, or your seat.
check: Can you balance on your seat?
lessons.try: Balance in three different shapes for five seconds each.

learn: Dynamic balance means keeping balance while moving.
Walking on a beam, riding a bike and skating use dynamic balance.
Keep your head up and arms out.
lessons.try: Walk heel-to-toe along a line forward and backward.

learn: Partners can balance together by leaning or pulling gently.
Counterbalance means leaning away while holding hands so you both stay up.
Communicate and go slowly.
check: When balancing with a partner, you should...
Can partners help each other balance?
lessons.try: Try a counterbalance with a partner: hold hands and lean back gently.

learn: Side to target, arm back like a letter L.
Step with the opposite foot, rotate your hips and throw.
Follow through toward the target.
check: Your throwing arm starts back like a...
lessons.try: Throw a ball at a wall target ten times using the cues.

learn: Ready hands: up and out in front.
Watch the ball into your hands.
Give with the ball: bend your elbows to soften it.
lessons.try: Catch a ball tossed at different heights ten times.

learn: To throw to a moving partner, throw ahead of them.
This is called leading the receiver.
Practise with a slow walker first.
check: To hit a moving target, throw...
lessons.try: Throw to a partner walking across the yard.

learn: Hold the handles with elbows close to your sides.
Turn the rope with your wrists.
Jump on the balls of your feet, just high enough to clear the rope.
lessons.try: Jump rope 20 times without stopping.

learn: Try jumping on one foot, alternating feet like running, or jumping side to side.
A criss-cross crosses your arms in front.
Start slowly before you try tricks fast.
check: Can you jump rope on one foot?
lessons.try: Learn one jump rope trick.

learn: In long rope, two turners swing the rope and jumpers run in.
Enter when the rope is going away from you and hits the ground.
Jump rope rhymes help keep the beat.
check: In long rope, who swings the rope?
When the rope hits the ground going away
lessons.try: Learn a jump rope rhyme like "Teddy bear, teddy bear, turn around".

learn: Your heart rate is how many times your heart beats in a minute.
You can feel your pulse on your wrist or neck.
Your heart rate goes up when you exercise and down when you rest.
check: How many times your heart beats in a minute
Where can you feel your pulse?
Exercise makes your heart rate go...
lessons.try: Count your pulse for 15 seconds before and after jumping jacks.

learn: Aerobic exercise makes you breathe harder for a long time.
Swimming, biking, dancing and running are aerobic.
It makes your heart and lungs stronger.
lessons.try: Do 10 minutes of aerobic exercise today.

learn: Fitness has parts: a strong heart, strong muscles and flexibility.
Push-ups and climbing build muscles. Stretching builds flexibility.
Children should be active at least 60 minutes a day.
check: How long should children be active each day?
lessons.try: Make a fitness plan for one week with one activity each day.

learn: Germs are tiny living things that can cause illness.
Washing hands with soap for 20 seconds removes most germs.
Wash before eating, after the toilet, after coughing and after playing outside.
check: How long should you wash hands?
lessons.try: Teach a younger child how to wash their hands.

learn: Brush twice a day for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste.
Floss to clean between teeth.
Visit the dentist for check-ups.
lessons.try: Brush and floss tonight, timing two minutes.

learn: Children your age need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep each night.
Too much screen time can take away from sleep and play.
Turn off screens at least an hour before bed.
check: How much sleep do children need?
Too much screen time can take away from...
lessons.try: Make a bedtime routine without screens.

learn: The five food groups are fruits, vegetables, grains, protein and dairy.
Each group helps the body in a different way.
A balanced meal has foods from several groups.
check: How many food groups are there?
A balanced meal has foods from...
lessons.try: Plan a dinner with at least four food groups.

learn: Food labels tell what's inside food.
Look for added sugar. Less is healthier.
Whole grains and fibre help you feel full and healthy.
lessons.try: Compare the sugar on two cereal boxes with a grown-up.

learn: Water is the best drink for your body.
Healthy snacks include fruit, vegetables, yogurt and nuts (if not allergic).
Some people have food allergies. Never share food without asking.
check: Why not share food without asking?
lessons.try: Make a list of five healthy snacks.

learn: Wear a helmet every time you ride.
Ride on the right side, with traffic, and use hand signals.
Stop and look at driveways and corners.
check: On the back of your head
Which side should you ride on?
lessons.try: Check your helmet: two fingers above eyebrows, straps in a V under ears, snug buckle.

learn: Always swim with a grown-up watching and near a lifeguard if possible.
Wear a life jacket on boats.
Use sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses on sunny days.
check: Who should watch when you swim?
lessons.try: Pack a beach or pool safety bag.

learn: Your body belongs to you. Safe touches feel okay. Unsafe touches make you feel uncomfortable.
Say no, get away and tell a trusted adult.
Secrets that make you feel bad should always be told to a trusted adult.
check: If a touch makes you uncomfortable, you...
Say no, get away and tell
Secrets that make you feel bad should be...
lessons.try: Name three trusted adults you could talk to.

learn: Feelings are signals from your body and mind.
You might feel a tight chest when worried or a warm face when embarrassed.
Naming a feeling helps you handle it.
check: What helps you handle a feeling?
A tight chest can mean you feel...
Signals from your body and mind
lessons.try: Draw a feelings chart with five faces and their names.

learn: A conflict is a disagreement.
Stop, calm down, talk about it using "I feel" words, and find a fair solution.
Options include taking turns, sharing or asking an adult.
lessons.try: Practise saying: "I feel upset when you take my turn. Can we take turns?"

learn: Empathy means understanding how someone else feels.
Notice when someone is left out or sad and offer help.
Small kindnesses, like a compliment, can make someone's day.
check: If someone is left out, you can...
lessons.try: Give three compliments today.
